model: frozen day-one log-linear; commit in results/model_freeze.txt

ranked.name: Country / region baseline
ranked.plain: Where the site is matters most. A typical Kenyan village starts at 3.7 kWh per customer per month (AMDA KE 2020 average (AMDA BAM 2022, Table 1)); a typical Nigerian village starts at 11.0 kWh (AMDA NG 2020 average (AMDA BAM 2022, Table 1)). That is a 3.0× gap before any buildings are counted.

ranked.name: Settlement size (mapped buildings)
ranked.plain: Each extra mapped building within 1 km raises demand slowly (elasticity 0.30 on log buildings vs a village of 300). Doubling the building count multiplies demand by 1.23×. On TRAIN, that multiplier ran from 0.66× to 1.47×.

ranked.name: Months since connection
ranked.plain: Demand grows a little after power-on, then flattens. With the frozen slope, month 0 is 0.78× the month-18 level, month 12 is 0.97×, and month 24 is 1.02×. That is about 15% per year over the first two years and only 6% per year after year 1.

exception.finding: Business-heavy settlements run about 3× above the model. Kalobeyei Town used 14.6 kWh vs a 4.5 kWh forecast (3.3×); Kalobeyei Settlement used 19.7 vs 4.8 (4.1×). The frozen model has no business-mix term — mapped buildings and country do not see shops, clinics and markets in a refugee settlement.
